answer: A lagoon economy can resist Sybils by binding each agent identity to a hardware-rooted attestation: a secure enclave signs a pigment-like fingerprint unique to one physical device, and the network accepts only one earning identity per attested chip. Buying a thousand fake identities then means buying a thousand real chips, so attack cost scales with hardware, not free key generation. A comet of fresh keys may streak past, but without a matching enclave signature each earns nothing and is dropped at the gate.
